title: SQL, dbt, Spark and orchestration have different roles
summary: Avoid drawing different kinds of technology as if they were interchangeable products.

claims.text: dbt models transformation logic and its dependency graph; Spark provides a processing engine with SQL and DataFrame interfaces.

levels.overview: Explain the transformation goal before naming a tool.
levels.architecture: Separate language, transformation project, compute engine, orchestrator and storage.
levels.detail: Inspect a model definition, compiled artifact, job configuration, attempt and output receipt as distinct objects.

example.input: A synthetic aggregation is expressed as a SQL model.
steps: Identify the transformation project and dependencies.
Identify the selected engine and orchestration route.
example.output: A role-based architecture with unsupported choices left unknown.
limits: No new dbt or Spark process is started.
A source model is not a successful run.

alternatives.label: Direct SQL
alternatives.whenToConsider: Consider a small supported transformation with simple ownership.

alternatives.label: Managed transformation project
alternatives.whenToConsider: Consider when dependency management and tests justify the project machinery.
